clue.text: Arabian woman about a hundred? Unlikely to be this!

parts.note: AR is a standard abbreviation for Arabic or Arabian

indicators.note: the woman's name goes round the other piece, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: Mandy is a woman's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A centenarian lady from Arabia is hardly going to be some rich man's glamorous companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a woman of about a hundred is unlikely to be decorative company on someone's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous companions taken to events for show are typically young, so a very old woman would hardly qualify.

clue.text: A Kipling lad, short boy having a sort of posture

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel

indicators.note: the word for boy is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: boy taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A young hero from Kipling, a small lad, striking some stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo is a stance with hands on hips and elbows out.

clue.text: Spite of one cold inside, masculine on the outside

indicators.note: the first pieces sit within the other word
the masculine word wraps round the rest

parts.note: male means masculine
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Spitefulness from a cold person within, macho on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, a desire to harm, the same as spite.

clue.text: State in line with America's avuncular image?

parts.note: as means in accordance with, as in 'as agreed'
Uncle Sam is the personification of the USA

explanation.surface: A state that fits the kindly uncle figure symbolising America.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for tea.

clue.text: Monster in den creating rupture

indicators.note: the monster goes inside the den word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy den or bar
an orc is a fantasy monster

explanation.surface: A beast in its lair causing a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorce is a split, a breaking of a marriage or other union.

clue.text: Fine cake containing cream primarily

indicators.note: the cake holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a scone is a small baked cake

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the word cream

explanation.surface: A delicate pastry with a dollop of cream in it, as at a cream tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective praising the cake, but it is a noun: at Oxford a sconce was a penalty imposed for breaches of table etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Oxford college custom a sconce was a forfeit or penalty, a kind of monetary punishment.

clue.text: French explorer wants cold meat without any embellishments

parts.note: ham is a meat
plain means unadorned

explanation.surface: An explorer from France just wants simple cold cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel de Champlain was the French explorer who founded Quebec.

clue.text: Bird not flying north, in roost having flown

indicators.note: these letters have scattered like birds leaving a perch

explanation.surface: A bird is not airborne going north, as the others in its roost have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not flying' belongs to the definition: the takahe is a flightless New Zealand bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Notornis is the genus of the takahe, a flightless rail of New Zealand.

clue.text: A tourer's abroad — having used this?

definitions.text: A tourer's abroad — having used this?

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the S

explanation.surface: A traveller is overseas, perhaps having taken a certain train.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-Channel train service carries travellers from London to the Continent.

clue.text: False exploitation traps four

indicators.note: the first word catches the numeral inside itself

parts.note: ill-use means mistreatment or exploitation
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A complaint that some exploitative scheme ensnares a group of four people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory or deceptive is not real, which is a synonym of false.

clue.text: Wilde right to be seen as sufferer for a cause?

parts.note: Marty Wilde is a British rock and roll singer of the 1950s and 60s

explanation.surface: Was Oscar Wilde rightly seen as someone who suffered for his principles?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Oscar Wilde; the Wilde needed is Marty Wilde, a British pop singer from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: One who endures persecution or death for a belief or cause is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Criticise young ladies needing to grow up

indicators.note: in a down entry, growing up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: gals are young women

explanation.surface: A rebuke for girls who must mature.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is British slang for running someone down, to criticise harshly.

clue.text: Like our Parliament Blair came to wreck

indicators.note: wrecking these letters means smashing them up into a new order

explanation.surface: Tony Blair arrived to ruin the British Parliament, a political jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK Parliament has two chambers, Commons and Lords, making it a two-chamber legislature.

clue.text: City couples getting a bit twisted inside

indicators.note: a small inner part of the word is turned about, swapping two of its central letters

parts.note: pairs are couples

explanation.surface: Romantic couples in a city getting slightly kinky behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit twisted inside' swaps the internal I and R of PAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital is a city, given here by a plain generic definition.

clue.text: Ray's nearest neighbours in the building

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, ray (re) sits between do and the following note
the note after ray in the sol-fa scale is me (mi)

explanation.surface: The people living closest to someone called Ray are in the same block.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray is the sol-fa note (do, ray, me...), not a person; the notes either side of it give the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a rounded vaulted structure, and by extension a building such as the Millennium Dome.

clue.text: Snakes etc. from India shop flogged

indicators.note: being flogged knocks the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Snakes and similar creatures sold off by an Indian store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' looks like British slang for sold, fitting the shop, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidians are members of the suborder of reptiles comprising serpents.

clue.text: Member of family has vermouth with a watery ice

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a family member
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Grandma drinks vermouth served over watery ice.
explanation.walkthrough: IT as Italian vermouth comes from the British bar order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is an Italian semi-frozen dessert of flavoured crushed ice.

clue.text: Being held in little credit makes Scottish poet more bad-tempered

indicators.note: the poet sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CR is a short form of credit
Rabbie is the Scots name for Robert Burns

explanation.surface: Getting little recognition makes a Scottish poet grumpier.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable, and the comparative form means more grumpy.

clue.text: A master keeps hold of dog? Quite the opposite if there's a tree

indicators.note: one piece contains the other
reverses the containment just stated, so the dog word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to dog is to follow, to track
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A master holds a dog's lead, or the reverse, and there is a tree nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarack is a North American larch, a coniferous tree.

clue.text: Travelled on unlikely flier, we hear — one making the journey difficult

indicators.note: signals the word is taken as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle
a hog is a pig, and 'pigs might fly' marks the impossible

explanation.surface: Someone rode on a creature that hardly ever flies and made a hard trip of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish motorist who hogs the road makes driving harder for everyone else.

clue.text: Humbug comes from manager with no hesitation

indicators.note: says the hesitation sound is dropped

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or football manager
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken by a boss who speaks without hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaff is old slang for nonsense or humbug, as in 'blow the gaff'.

clue.text: Not getting runs, old-fashioned rabbit

indicators.note: says the letter for runs is left out of the word

parts.note: corny means dated or old-fashioned
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dated rabbit that fails to score in a game of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Cony is an old word for a rabbit, still used in heraldry and the Bible.

clue.text: Greek character holding princess up in Indian city

indicators.note: the Greek letter contains the other piece

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the name reads bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A Greek lifting a princess aloft in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chennai, formerly Madras, is a major city on India's east coast.

clue.text: Writer with fury wanting rid of Queen and State

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: says the queen's letters are removed

parts.note: anger is fury
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An author enraged and wanting to be rid of the monarchy and the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is a state of Malaysia, an island and part of the mainland.

clue.text: It sounds like a novelist of the eighteenth century's back

indicators.note: signals that the spoken form gives the entry

parts.words: a novelist of the eighteenth century
parts.note: the indefinite article, A; Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy in the eighteenth century

explanation.surface: The rear end of an eighteenth-century writer is being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term for at or toward the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Black Country not particularly interesting?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Is the Black Country, the industrial West Midlands region of England, rather dull?
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is the industrial area west of Birmingham; here the two words simply give their own pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bland is dull and lacking flavour or excitement.

clue.text: Impetuosity and ire somehow limited by endless tact

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are enclosed by the trimmed word
the word for tact loses its final letter

parts.note: finesse is delicate tact

indicators.note: the letters of ire are muddled in some way

explanation.surface: Rashness and anger held in check by a diplomat whose tact keeps running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link here; FINESSE as 'tact' is the delicate, diplomatic sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery temperament means passion and rashness, so the quality is close to impetuosity.

clue.text: Special fluid gets one menial task cut short

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the task loses its final letter

parts.note: a chore is a menial task

explanation.surface: An unusual liquid comes with a lowly job abandoned early.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of gods.

clue.text: I keep quiet, absorbing excellent article in book

indicators.note: the hush takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: sh is the command to keep quiet
A1 means excellent, written AI
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent while taking in a fine piece of writing in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Island with nothing had to be developed? Definitely not!

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
O is zero, nothing
ate means had, as with a meal

explanation.surface: An island with nothing on it was to be built up? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: something only just begun is the opposite of developed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means rudimentary or only partly formed, so certainly not developed.

clue.text: Jaunty artist with drunkard's way of expressing affection?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a drunk would slur 'kiss' into something like this

explanation.surface: A cheerful painter, tipsy, offering a sloppy kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish look is dashing and debonair, with a cocky jauntiness.

clue.text: Element from the North diminished and re-expanded

definitions.text: Element from the North diminished and re-expanded

parts.words: Element from the North diminished and re-expanded
parts.note: North shrinks to its one-letter abbreviation, which is then grown again by reading it as a chemical symbol

explanation.walkthrough: Shorten North to N, then 're-expand' N as if it were the atomic symbol it also is.
explanation.definitionFit: The gas making up most of the air is a chemical element whose symbol is N.
